title: Adaptive client retry presets with per-route idempotency hints and streaming resume tokens
creator: Nadia Kapoor
description:
Motivation: SDK clients across Python/TypeScript/Go need a shared, opinionated surface for retries and idempotency that balances safety (no accidental duplicates) with reliability (recover from transient infra failures). Existing tickets cover retry taxonomies and idempotency separately; this task proposes a pragmatic, cross-language runtime API and defaults focused on developer ergonomics and streaming use-cases (resume tokens/checkpoints).

Goal: Define and implement a cross-SDK RetryPolicy and IdempotencyHint primitives, default presets per-route (stateless calls vs long-running streamed calls), mapping from transport errors to retry categories, and examples for Python/TS/Go. Provide hooks for operators to tune per-customer latency/cost SLOs while keeping safe defaults for most apps.

High-level design:
- RetryPolicy (cross-sdk surface): max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, backoff_multiplier, jitter ("decorrelated" | "full" | "none"), retry_on (list of canonical retry categories), allow_idempotency_hint_override (bool).
- IdempotencyHint: an SDK-level header/metadata helper that documents intent ("idempotent","non-idempotent","at_least_once_optional"). SDKs provide helpers to generate stable idempotency keys (timestamped UUID v1-like) and a utility to attach them to request objects and to persist them for retries/resends.
- Streaming resume tokens: for streamed generation or long-running multi-chunk responses, servers may return a resume token after each committed checkpoint. SDKs will expose a ResumeToken type (opaque string) and an automatic checkpointing policy (checkpoint every N tokens or M seconds). On failure, SDKs will attempt to resume using the last successful token under the same idempotency key.

Default presets (recommended):
- Short stateless calls (embeddings, simple generation < 2s): max_attempts=4, initial_backoff_ms=150, backoff_multiplier=2.0, max_backoff_ms=10000, jitter=decorrelated, retry_on=[TRANSIENT_NETWORK, HTTP_5XX_EXCEPT_501, RATE_LIMIT].
- Idempotent heavy calls (mutating-safe endpoints where idempotency key provided): max_attempts=6, initial_backoff_ms=100, backoff_multiplier=1.5, max_backoff_ms=15000, jitter=decorrelated, retry_on=[TRANSIENT_NETWORK, HTTP_5XX_ALL, RATE_LIMIT].
- Streaming sessions: max_attempts=3 (per-resume), initial_backoff_ms=200, backoff_multiplier=1.4, max_backoff_ms=8000, checkpoint_interval_tokens=1024, resume_grace_period_seconds=300. If resume fails repeatedly, fall back to fresh session with user-visible error indicating potential duplication risk.

Error taxonomy (canonicalized across SDKs):
- TRANSIENT_NETWORK: DNS failures, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, connection refused transient. Safe to retry with backoff.
- HTTP_5XX_ALL: 500-599 server errors. Retryable, but 501/505 treated as non-retryable (server does not implement/unsupported).
- RATE_LIMIT: 429 or quota signals. Retry but use server-supplied Retry-After when present and escalate jitter.
- AUTH_FAILURE: 401/403/token invalid. Non-retryable; trigger token refresh flows only if SDK can safely refresh without user action.
- CLIENT_ERROR: 4xx non-auth and non-rate-limit (400/404). Generally non-retryable.
- STREAM_PARTIAL_COMMIT: stream-level partial commit detected on connection loss where server indicates progress checkpoint exists. Resume semantics apply.

Mapping to transport errors: SDKs normalize platform errors into these canonical categories (examples: Node fetch ECONNRESET -> TRANSIENT_NETWORK; Python requests 504 -> HTTP_5XX_ALL). The normalization table will be part of each SDK's transport layer and tested under CI.

Idempotency semantics:
- Default: SDKs will not retry non-idempotent calls automatically unless an explicit idempotency key is supplied or the developer opts into "allow_unsafe_retries" for local dev.
- Idempotency key format: opaque string, recommended generation with a stable prefix + RFC4122 UUIDv1 to enable server-side ordering heuristics. SDK helper: IdempotencyKey.generate(context="upload"), which returns a string and stores it in the request metadata for automatic re-use on retries.
- Per-route hint: SDKs ship a small metadata file mapping API route -> recommended idempotency hint (idempotent by default for read/embedding routes; non-idempotent for mutation endpoints). This allows auto-attach for common patterns while giving full override to developers.

Cross-language API sketch (conceptual, not binding):
- RetryPolicy(policy_name="balanced", max_attempts=4, initial_backoff_ms=150, ...)
- client.request(route="/v1/generate", body, retry_policy=RetryPolicy.PRESET.BALANCED, idempotency_key=IdempotencyKey.generate("chat-turn"))
- streaming = client.stream_generate(..., checkpoint_callback=save_token_fn, resume_token=previous_token)

Backward compatibility and migration: SDKs should default to conservative presets on major version bumps and log telemetry about default changes. Admins can set tenant-level policy overrides via console or environment variables.

Observability: Emit metrics on retry_count, last_retry_reason (canonical category), resumed_sessions, resume_failures, and idempotency_key_reuse_count. Link metrics to Console dashboards and add an alert if resume_failures spike above threshold for a model/route.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-language RetryPolicy object implemented in Python/TS/Go with same field names and documented semantics
Default presets added to all three SDKs and enabled in CI tests that simulate canonical transport errors
IdempotencyKey helper implemented and integrated into client.request paths with opt-out flag
Streaming resume token format and checkpoint policy implemented with example in Python + TS + Go samples
Telemetry emitted for retry categories and resume attempts and dashboard template created
decisions: Use decorrelated jitter as default jitter strategy (best tradeoff between thundering herd and tail latency)
Do not auto-retry non-idempotent routes unless explicit idempotency key is provided
Resume tokens treated as opaque by SDKs and persisted only by client code or optional SDK store; SDK provides convenience in-memory persistence for short-lived clients
technical_notes: We must add canonical error mapping layers in each SDK transport adapter to keep retry logic platform-agnostic
Python SDK will expose a small file routes_idempotency_hints.json shipped with the package; TS/Go will have equivalent maps

Streaming checkpoints rely on server contract: server must return 'X-Resume-Token' or include token in stream envelope. If not present, resume attempted only if server returns explicit STREAM_PARTIAL_COMMIT category
Rate-limit handling should prefer server Retry-After header when present and fall back to exponential backoff with capped jitter
